items.title: USA Pickleball will retire six OWL Sport quiet paddles from sanctioned play on Feb. 1, 2028 after spin-test findings
items.summary: USA Pickleball said Nov. 9 that six OWL Sport paddle models (Talon X1, CX, CXE, PX, PXE and SILENT STORM) show performance that improves with use, which it calls 'Degrade to Benefit,' based on evaluation following its new Spin Rate Test (in effect since Oct. 1, 2026). The paddles stay approved during a transition period through Jan. 31, 2028; starting Feb. 1, 2028 they will no longer be approved for USA Pickleball-sanctioned competition. USA Pickleball credited OWL Sport's work on noise, and OWL Sport is developing updated Quiet Category paddles that will go through standard certification.

items.title: Study: pickleball arm and shoulder injuries skew toward women and players over 60, and fractures are the most common
items.summary: A descriptive study reported by Healio estimated 14,916 pickleball-related upper-extremity injuries in U.S. emergency-department data from 2014 to 2023. Players over 60 accounted for 83.1% and women for 59%. Fractures were the most common injury (58.6%, versus 36.1% of comparable tennis injuries), and the shoulder (36.4%) and forearm (34%) were the most-injured areas. Injury incidence per 100,000 players peaked in 2021 at 62.74, versus 5.27 in 2015 and 30.6 in 2022.

items.summary: Indoor pickleball company The Picklr (parent Picklr, Inc., and Picklr Clubs, Inc.) filed Chapter 11 in Dallas on Oct. 9; per Bankruptcy Observer the franchisor entity did not file. Financing is led by franchisee Tom Neale's Dynamus Alliance. Per a bankruptcy docket tracker, the court is set to consider final approval of a $4.365 million financing facility on Nov. 10, and the U.S. Trustee and a landlord have filed objections. The loan sets milestones tied to a sale of franchise agreements, which that source estimates at about Nov. 23 for sale pleadings, Dec. 23 for a plan and sale order, and Jan. 7, 2027 for closing. The creditors' meeting is Nov. 18. Franchised clubs are not themselves debtors, and no buyer has been announced.

items.title: Gear: USA Pickleball delists the CPX Hyper+ elongated 14mm and 16mm paddles after retail samples failed compliance testing
items.summary: USA Pickleball has removed the CPX Hyper+ elongated 14mm and 16mm models from its certified paddle list after courtside testing and market sampling found significant differences in PBCoR and deflection between the paddles submitted for certification and mass-production units sold to players. USA Pickleball's Nov. 2 equipment statement says it is working with CPX on new versions under a new model name. CPX's own Hyper+ update page says some recent production units played hotter than the certified samples, that current Hyper+ paddles are not for USA Pickleball-sanctioned events, and that a Hyper+ 2 is in recertification with dual factory/warehouse testing and serial numbers planned. The Dink, reporting Nov. 5 from the USA Pickleball Nationals in San Diego, says officials told paddle reviewer John Kew that potential financial penalties against CPX are 'in consideration.' No fines have been announced. Rec play is unaffected; tournament players who need an approved paddle can request a Hyper+ 2 swap once it is available, per CPX.

items.title: Eye safety: Singapore doctors report pickleball eye injuries as U.S. data shows older players at higher risk
items.summary: The Straits Times reports that Singapore hospitals have treated pickleball eye injuries from direct ball hits, including retinal breaks that needed laser treatment and a dislocated lens implant that needed surgery, though doctors there say cases can't be counted reliably. Doctors advise protective eyewear and urgent eye checks after any hit; one sports scientist notes injuries are rising mainly because more people are playing.

items.title: Noise fight: Walnut Creek's Rudgear Park pickleball dispute enters its fourth year in court
items.summary: Neighbors of Rudgear Park in Walnut Creek, Calif. are asking a judge to make the city control noise from eight pickleball courts converted from two tennis courts, Patch reports. Their amended complaint says homes sit 50 to 90 feet from the courts and alleges noise up to 88 decibels; they want fewer courts, quieter equipment, soundproofing, player limits or removal. The city says it cut court hours about 20%, closes the courts two afternoons a week and locks them outside posted hours, and won't comment on the litigation. Players told the council it's 'a community park,' not a quiet meadow.

items.title: Club shakeout: Bisnow says pickleball's retail bet is souring, a Wake Forest club is sued over rent, and CityPickle questions franchising
items.summary: Bisnow reports that some pickleball clubs that leased mall and big-box space are struggling as markets saturate, pointing to The Picklr's Oct. 9 bankruptcy filing (about $19 million in liabilities across 76 franchise locations, per Bisnow) and rents of roughly $30,000 to $50,000 a month for a 10-court club. It also notes that participation is still rising: SFIA counts more than 24 million players last year, up from nearly 20 million in 2024. The Triangle Business Journal reports a landlord has sued Pickles and Play over about $80,000 in unpaid rent at its Wake Forest, N.C. location, after the operator closed another Triangle facility earlier this year. In The Dink, CityPickle co-founder Mary Cannon argues that suburban clubs are hyper-local businesses and asks whether the franchise model adds value, since rent and labor are set locally.

items.title: Bossier City bystanders, including a Barksdale AFB medic, honored for saving a player who collapsed at a pickleball facility
items.summary: Gary Rondeau, a retired Air Force firefighter and EMT who is now the medical emergency manager at Barksdale Air Force Base's medical treatment facility, and other bystanders received the Bossier City Fire Department's Life Saving Award, the first time the department has given it in 15 years, according to a DVIDS release. Bruce Poynter collapsed in cardiac arrest at an indoor pickleball facility in Bossier City, La. on July 8. Bystanders including Dylan Fauver and Dr. Sean Patel started CPR, a police officer used an AED, and EMS took over. Per the release, Poynter has no lasting effects, and he and his wife have since become CPR certified.

items.title: Courts watch: Champaign doubles to 16 courts this Saturday; Lewes, Del. indoor complex opposition softens
items.summary: Champaign, Ill.'s John Street pickleball complex at 2203 W. John St. grows from 8 to 16 courts and is expected to open Saturday, Oct. 31, the News-Gazette reports. The roughly $2.2 million phase adds shade over four courts, restrooms and parking, with a grand opening Nov. 14 from 10 a.m. to noon, per WCIA. In Delaware, neighbor opposition to the Dave Marshall Tennis & Pickleball expansion near Lewes softened at the Oct. 27 Sussex County Council hearing after negotiations, Spotlight Delaware reports. Proposed conditions include indoor-only pickleball, 15 tournaments a year and limited hours; the project has a $1 million state Sports Tourism grant and plans 5 indoor courts. A final vote is likely Nov. 17.
